summary:
ANTIGRAVITY is a health monitoring system for astronauts. It has a web dashboard, a real-time backend and an iPhone + Apple Watch app, and all three share one data contract.

What we developed: The system tracks heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, blood glucose, sleep, mood and radiation dose. It shows each reading as green, amber or red on live charts, a clickable body map and a cabin-environment view. A Gemini-powered assistant explains each result in plain language. It says why a measurement matters, what to do, and when to contact the flight surgeon. It also warns proactively, with popups, voice and phone alerts, and turns the alert steps into tasks.

How it addresses the challenge: It collects health indicators from several inputs (watch, phone, manual entry) and presents them visually. It gives actionable guidance for self-assessment far from Earth. Thresholds and multi-day trend rules decide the status colors. The AI never does, so the status stays predictable and safe.

Why it matters: On Artemis and Mars missions, communication with the ground is delayed and astronauts must judge their own health. Early, understandable warnings can prevent a minor issue from becoming critical.
details:
What it does and how it works

ANTIGRAVITY collects an astronaut's health indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep, mood and radiation dose. It turns them into a clear green / amber / red status. Data comes from an Apple Watch (live heart rate and a quick mood check-in), an iPhone, manual entry, or an AI chat bot that logs readings. All clients share one JSON data contract.

A zero-dependency Node.js relay holds the data in memory and streams every change over Server-Sent Events (SSE) to all connected devices at once. A web dashboard shows crew status cards, 7-day time-series charts, a clickable body map and a cabin-environment view (O2, CO2, pressure, temperature, humidity, radiation). A rules engine checks thresholds and multi-day trends. When a reading crosses a limit, the system raises an alert before anyone asks. It shows a popup, speaks the alert, and pushes it to every affected phone. The alert steps become tasks, with at most three per astronaut.

Benefits

- Astronauts understand their health without medical training. Each result explains why it matters, what to do, and when to call the flight surgeon.

- Alerts reach the whole crew at the same moment.

- The system keeps working offline. If the backend is unreachable, the clients fall back to local mock data.

Intended impact

On Artemis and Mars missions, communication with Earth is delayed and astronauts must assess themselves. We want to help them catch problems early and act on them, so a small issue does not become critical.

Tools and technology

- Web: Vite, React, TypeScript, three.js, hosted on Vercel.

- Backend: Node.js (type-stripping), SSE, hosted on Render.

- AI: Google Gemini, called only from the server so the key stays private. A rule-based fallback runs when the API is unavailable.

- Mobile: Swift and SwiftUI for iPhone 16 Pro and watchOS, synced with WatchConnectivity.

- Hardware: iPhone and Apple Watch.

- Process: Playwright for end-to-end tests, Git and GitHub with pull requests, and written Architecture Decision Records.

Creativity

- Alerts are proactive. The AI speaks first instead of waiting for a question.

- It spans watch, phone and web, with real-time fan-out to several phones.

- It replays historical incident scenarios and runs live simulations.

- It includes a 3D body map and a voice interface.

Factors we considered

- Safety: The AI never decides the status color. Deterministic thresholds do, so the result is predictable and explainable. The UI states clearly that this is a demo, not a medical device.

- Privacy: The AI key stays server-side, and the project holds no real personal health data.

- Reliability: A stage demo cannot depend on Wi-Fi, so every client has an offline path.

- Scope: With six people and about 24 hours, we chose a working demo over a complex architecture.

- Accessibility: The language is plain, and the UI is in Turkish for our team.
